output.review_comment:
Requesting changes. The code passes all 9 tests, but it adds a rule the documented contract doesn't allow, and the PR doesn't say so.

What's right:
- Mixed-case words (NASA, iPhone) are now kept as written, including when one starts the title. This was the real bug on main, where every word went through capitalize().
- A small word at the end of a title is now capitalized ("Waiting For"), as docstring rule 2 requires.
- Trailing punctuation is handled correctly ("Come in, Sit Down").

The problem: the PR adds a new rule that capitalizes a small word right after a word ending in ':'. The docstring doesn't allow this. Rule 2 says a small word is lowercase unless it is the first or last word of the text, so "notes from the field: a year of remote work" should give "Field: a Year", but test_subtitle_after_colon expects "Field: A Year". The test and the docstring conflict, and the agent quietly went with the test. The docstring still describes the old behavior, and with no PR description, nobody is told about the conflict.

The colon rule is probably the intended editorial spec, but before merge:
1. Add the subtitle/colon rule to the title_case docstring. Say exactly what counts as a subtitle marker: only ':', or also '?' and '!'.
2. Add a PR description that explains the conflict, so the team can confirm the colon rule is really what editorial wants.
3. Optional: checking words[index - 1].endswith(':') is clearer than result[-1].rstrip(), and the rstrip() is redundant anyway.
